answer: An agent's k-th identity under one operator must lock a bond of 10 × 2^(k−1) credits, so each sibling key doubles the price of the last. Admission runs through a shared orchard ledger where every newcomer must extend an existing thread of attestations and pass a sonnet-length challenge in 90 seconds, verified by a stake-weighted quorum. A farm of 1,000 fakes would need about 2^1000 credits, so bulk scaling collapses long before any single identity becomes cheap.
